headline: Global stocks tumble amid AI panic after US midterm election results
summary: Fears over Democratic Party policies impacting AI investment have wiped $3.2 trillion off the US stock market, with Asian markets also seeing significant drops.
details: US stock markets saw over $3.2 trillion wiped off yesterday, with the Nasdaq tech index plummeting 5.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 3.44%, and the S&P 500 lost 4.36% in a broad sell-off.

This market turmoil stems from fears that the Democratic Party's midterm election success will negatively impact the AI investment boom. Asia-Pacific markets also experienced significant losses, with Japan's Nikkei down nearly 6%, South Korea's KOSPI falling 6.7%, and Taiwan's TAIEX dropping 4.5%.

Christopher Forbes of CMC Markets described the market action as "a bit of a disaster," noting widespread client margin calls. He explained that investors are reacting to a perceived "policy and six-year structural shift" that could cool AI, data centers, and related approvals.

Memory chip makers, key beneficiaries of the AI boom, were among the hardest hit. SanDisk slumped 22%, while Micron and AMD both saw their values decrease by 17%. Chip giant Nvidia also led fallers on the DJIA, down over 9%.

Analysts attribute the sell-off to policy uncertainty, as Democrats are seen as more critical of data centers, potentially slowing AI investment rollout. This comes amid existing public opposition to the sector and concerns about tech regulation.

The "AI trade" was already on shaky ground, with recent "Magnificent Seven" earnings undershooting growth expectations. These results had already signaled a potential slowdown in the pace of AI spending, contributing to investor caution.
